mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines the inertia of motion?

options.A: The tendency of a moving object to continue moving at a constant speed in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
options.B: The tendency of an object to remain at rest unless a force is applied.
options.C: The resistance of an object to any change in its shape.
options.D: The force that slows down a moving object.

mcqs.answer: The tendency of a moving object to continue moving at a constant speed in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of motion is the property that makes a moving body keep moving in the same direction and speed unless a net external force acts on it. Option B describes inertia of rest, C describes elasticity, and D describes friction, not inertia.

mcqs.question: When a car suddenly takes a sharp turn, which effect of inertia of direction is observed?

options.A: The car tends to continue moving straight, causing it to skid outward.
options.B: The car immediately follows the new curved path without any lateral motion.
options.D: The car accelerates forward along the turn.

mcqs.answer: The car tends to continue moving straight, causing it to skid outward.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of direction resists a change in the direction of motion. When the car turns, the passengers and the vehicle body tend to keep moving in the original straight line, leading to outward skidding. The other options do not reflect this resistance to change in direction.

mcqs.question: Which of the following situations best illustrates inertia of motion in everyday life?

options.A: A ball rolling on a smooth floor keeps moving until it hits a wall.
options.B: A book lying undisturbed on a table.
options.C: A stretched rubber band snapping back to its original shape.

mcqs.answer: A ball rolling on a smooth floor keeps moving until it hits a wall.
mcqs.explanation: The rolling ball continues its motion due to inertia of motion and only stops when an external force (the wall) acts on it. Option B shows inertia of rest, C shows elasticity, and D is a phase‑change process, none of which demonstrate inertia of motion.

mcqs.question: A passenger feels thrown forward when a bus suddenly stops. Which concept best explains this observation?
mcqs.explanation: The passenger's body tends to remain in its state of motion (moving forward) when the bus stops, illustrating inertia. Momentum is related but does not directly explain the sensation; gravity acts vertically, and friction opposes motion, not cause the forward throw.

mcqs.question: Identify the incorrect statement about inertia of rest.

options.A: An object at rest will stay at rest unless a net external force acts on it.
options.B: Inertia of rest is the same as friction.
options.C: An object at rest will start moving on its own if left undisturbed.
options.D: A stationary ball on a flat surface remains stationary until pushed.

mcqs.answer: An object at rest will start moving on its own if left undisturbed.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of rest means a stationary object remains stationary unless acted upon by an external force. Option C contradicts this principle, making it the false statement. Options A and D correctly describe inertia of rest, while B confuses it with friction.

mcqs.question: A hockey puck slides on ice and eventually comes to rest. Which factor primarily overcomes its inertia of motion?

options.C: Friction between the puck and ice

mcqs.answer: Friction between the puck and ice
mcqs.explanation: The puck's motion is stopped by the frictional force acting opposite to its direction of travel, which provides the external force needed to change its state of motion. Gravity acts vertically, air resistance is negligible on ice, and magnetic forces are irrelevant here.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares inertia of direction with inertia of rest?

options.A: Both refer to an object's tendency to change its speed.
options.B: Inertia of direction resists a change in the direction of motion, whereas inertia of rest resists a change from rest to motion.
options.C: Inertia of direction applies only to stationary objects.
options.D: Inertia of rest is about resisting changes in direction while moving.

mcqs.answer: Inertia of direction resists a change in the direction of motion, whereas inertia of rest resists a change from rest to motion.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of direction deals with the resistance to altering the path of a moving object, while inertia of rest deals with the resistance to initiating motion from a stationary state. Options A, C, and D misrepresent these definitions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of inertia?

options.A: A ball rolling down an inclined plane speeds up as it descends.
options.B: A book remains on a table until you push it.
options.C: A passenger continues moving forward when a car stops suddenly.
options.D: A soccer ball keeps rolling after being kicked until friction stops it.

mcqs.answer: A ball rolling down an inclined plane speeds up as it descends.
mcqs.explanation: The ball’s acceleration down the slope is due to the component of gravitational force along the plane, not because of inertia. Options B, C, and D all illustrate inertia: resistance to change in state of rest or motion.
